entradas.text: I rushed past the guards to my door.
entradas.menu: Don't look at them and go to your door.

entradas.text: I didn't know if it was my imagination, but there seemed to be more guards outside my complex than usual.
The usual crowd of protesters was waiting for me outside the gates of the complex.
The guards formed a cordon to let me through.
I hurried past them, went inside and locked the front door behind me. I heard hesitant footsteps coming my way.
Once inside, I locked the front door behind me.
I regarded them with suspicion as I passed. With the military against me, could they be trusted?
entradas.menu: Give the guards a suspicious look.

entradas.text: "Hi, Papa."
I opened my arms to embrace my daughter. She reluctantly accepted.
entradas.menu: Hug her.

entradas.text: "Deana! How is school?"
entradas.menu: "Deana! How is school?"

entradas.text: "Where's your mother?"
entradas.menu: "Where's your mother?"

entradas.text: Deana mutely gestured towards the kitchen.
"I'll be in my room till dinner."
Deana shrugged.
"I won a prize at the science fair. Honestly, I think they were teaching girls different stuff before 'cause they knew we were smarter than boys."
"I won a prize at the handicrafts fair. Mama didn't seem to care that much, though."
"You might be right."
entradas.menu: "You might be right."

entradas.text: "That's just silly."
entradas.menu: "That's just silly."

entradas.text: "Well, *I* care."
entradas.menu: "Well, *I* care."

entradas.text: "She's just jealous because she was always bad at sewing."
entradas.menu: "She's just jealous because she was always bad at sewing."

entradas.text: "How's school?"
entradas.menu: "How's school?"

entradas.text: "Where's your mother?"
entradas.menu: "Where's your mother?"

entradas.text: Deana ignored my comment and gestured vaguely towards the kitchen.
"Mama's in there. I'll be up in my room till dinner."
I followed her with my eyes as she went upstairs, thinking about the days when she idolized me. She was starting to look more and more like her mother.
I hesitantly stepped into the kitchen. Monica was stirring a pot on the stove, her back turned to me.
I snuck up behind Monica and gave her a hug. She screamed and dropped her ladle.
entradas.menu: Hug her from behind.

entradas.text: "Smells delicious."
entradas.menu: "Smells delicious."

entradas.text: I walked back out and went to wait for Franc in the living room. I didn't want to disturb her.
entradas.menu: Walk back out and wait for Franc in the living room.

entradas.text: Monica whirled around in surprise. Her eyes narrowed.
"God, Anton, don't startle me like that! You know we're all still on edge after the parade."
"God, Anton, don't startle me like that! Go wait in the living room. I'll tell you when dinner's ready."
"I'm sorry. I'll go wait in the living room."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. I'll go wait in the living room."

entradas.text: "Can't a man greet his wife?"
entradas.menu: "Can't a man greet his wife?"

entradas.text: "No. Not if he's you."
I walked back out and sat on the living room sofa.
I awkwardly flipped through one of Monica's women's magazines. I felt like an intruder in my own home.
Suddenly, Franc burst through the door.
"Well, I'd be more suspicious of them if I were you."
"Sorry I'm late. Are some of those guards outside new? I had to convince them I was really your son."
"You could've invited them in. There's enough food."
entradas.menu: "You could've invited them in. There's enough food."

entradas.text: "Sorry I'm late. I ran into a couple of my friends protesting outside. It was pretty awkward, telling them I was having dinner with you."
"They might be."
entradas.menu: "They might be."

entradas.text: He flung his backpack in a corner and sprawled out in a chair.
"I'm starting to get suspicious of them, to be honest."
entradas.menu: "I'm starting to get suspicious of them, to be honest."

entradas.text: "Ha. Even if they would cross the picket line, they're vegetarians."
"Sorry I'm late. I was with Sheyna. We were, uh, studying."
"Don't do it. They brought goggles."
"You *know* those brats? I was going to ask the guards to have them tear-gassed."
entradas.menu: "You *know* those brats? I was going to ask the guards to have them tear-gassed."

entradas.text: "I hope you two are being careful."
entradas.menu: "I hope you two are being careful."

entradas.text: "So that's still going on."
entradas.menu: "So that's still going on."

entradas.text: "Yes, no thanks to you. One of her uncles was almost killed during that business at the dam."
"We're certainly being more careful than you've been with your treatment of her people."
"Don't you worry. I've seen what fatherhood does to a man."
"Don't look so surprised."
Franc smirked. He looked like he was about to say something else, but then Deana came down the stairs.
Franc glared at me. He looked like he was about to say something else, but then Deana came down the stairs.
He flung his backpack in a corner and sprawled out in a chair.
He flung his backpack in a corner and sprawled out in a chair.
"Shit, Dad, that parade was a close call. I thought the ball was bad..."
"Language!"
entradas.menu: "Language!"

entradas.text: "It wasn't a 'close call' for Serge."
entradas.menu: "It wasn't a 'close call' for Serge."

entradas.text: "I know. I can't believe he's gone."
"You almost died *again*, and your biggest concern is swear words?"
"Serge is dead, and your biggest concern is swear words?"
"I know. I still can't believe nobody was hurt."
entradas.menu: "I know. I still can't believe nobody was hurt."

entradas.text: "This time."
Before I could respond, Deana came running down the stairs.
Deana came running down the stairs.
"Franc!"
"Hey, pipsqueak."
He ruffled her hair. I thought about how much time had passed since we'd all been together under one roof.
Monica emerged from the kitchen and gave Franc a big hug. As she turned back to me, the warmth drained from her face.
"Dinner's ready."
The four of us gathered around the dining room table. Monica ladled out bowls full of beef stew -- not my favorite, but a comforting dish nonetheless.
"Now that we're all here, I wanted to say something."
entradas.menu: "Now that we're all here, I wanted to say something."

entradas.text: I raised my glass for a toast. Monica, Franc and Deana slowly followed suit, looking puzzled.
entradas.menu: Raise your glass.

entradas.text: I tapped on the side of my glass for attention. Monica, Franc and Deana looked at me.
entradas.menu: Tap on the side of your glass.

entradas.text: "I know the past four years have been hard on all of us."
entradas.menu: "I know the past four years have been hard on all of us."

entradas.text: "The past four years have been the hardest in my life."
entradas.menu: "The past four years have been the hardest in my life."

entradas.text: "The past four years have tested our strength as a family."
entradas.menu: "The past four years have tested our strength as a family."

entradas.text: "I was so busy focusing on the needs of the Sordish people that I forgot about Sordland's most important people: my own wife and children."
entradas.menu: "I was so busy focusing on the needs of the Sordish people that I forgot about Sordland's most important people: my own family."

entradas.text: "I let my power get to my head. I became unrecognizable to myself -- and to all of you."
entradas.menu: "I let my power get to my head. I became unrecognizeable to myself -- and to all of you."

entradas.text: "I've done some unforgivable things. Especially to you, Monica."
entradas.menu: "I've done some unforgivable things. Especially to you, Monica."

entradas.text: "I hope I can redeem myself someday."
entradas.menu: "I hope I can redeem myself someday."

entradas.text: "I hope someday, we'll be able to put this behind us and be a family again."
entradas.menu: "I hope someday, we'll be able to put this behind us and be a family again."

entradas.text: Monica looked at me sadly. She slowly shook her head.
"I swear to you all, I'll learn from my mistakes during my next term."
entradas.menu: "I swear to you all, I'll learn from my mistakes during my next term."

entradas.text: "As a first step towards that, I'm retiring from politics at the end of this term."
entradas.menu: "As a first step towards that, I'm retiring from politics at the end of this term."

entradas.text: "But right now, there's no time. We need to get out of Sordland. All of us."
entradas.menu: "But right now, there's no time. We need to get out of Sordland. All of us."

entradas.text: "I swear to you all, once I'm retired things will go back to the way they used to be."
entradas.menu: "I swear to you all, once I'm retired things will go back to the way they used to be."

entradas.text: "My retirement from politics is going to be the best thing that ever happened to us."
entradas.menu: "My retirement from politics is going to be the best thing that ever happened to us."

entradas.text: Everyone turned to look at me in shock.
"Anton, what in the everloving hell?"
"I've just signed part of my own country over to Rumburg. I'm going to be a pariah, and so are all of you."
entradas.menu: "I've just signed part of my own country over to Rumburg. I'm going to be a pariah, and so are all of you."

entradas.text: "I'm about to be the first president in Sordish history to get impeached. I'll be a pariah, and so will all of you."
entradas.menu: "I'm about to be the first president in Sordish history to get impeached. I'll be a pariah, and so will all of you."

entradas.text: "The military is after me. After what happened at the parade, I'm not safe -- and neither are any of you."
entradas.menu: "The military is after me. After what happened at the parade, I'm not safe -- and neither are any of you."

entradas.text: Deana frowned.
"What's a pariah?"
"It's an outcast, Dee. Like what I am since everyone at Holsord State found out how I really got in."
Franc gave me a pointed look. Deana still looked uncertain.
"It's an outcast, Dee. Like what I am since Anton Rayne became the enemy of Holsord State."
"It's an outcast, Dee."
"We're supposed to uproot our entire lives because you screwed up?"
Deana looked at me in disbelief. Her lower lip trembled slightly.
Monica slammed a hand down on the table. We all turned to look at her.
"Mama? Is that true?"
"Are they gonna kill us like they killed Serge?"
"Are they gonna try to kill us like they tried to kill Papa?"
"Nobody's going anywhere. Except you, Anton."
"Franc, Deana -- your father and I are getting divorced."
"What a surprise."
Monica scowled at me.
"No, sweetie. Your father's imagining things."
"The only person in danger is him."
"I'm not surprised, Franc. He hasn't been living in the house for weeks."
"Yeah, that was sarcasm."
Everyone at the table looked at me in shock.
"Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."
entradas.menu: "Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."

entradas.text: "Monica, now is not the time. We've got to get out of here."
entradas.menu: "Monica, now is not the time. We've got to get out of here."

entradas.text: "Your mother is right. We're divorcing immediately after the election."
entradas.menu: "Your mother is right. We're divorcing immediately after the election."

entradas.text: "That was the plan before I learned the truth about what you'd done with your time in office. Along with the rest of Sordland."
"No, Anton. You've dug your own grave. You've got to deal with this yourself."
She looked up. Her face was dead serious.
"Go, Anton. I think it's better this way."
"No. Not without my family."
entradas.menu: "No. Not without my family."

entradas.text: "You're not even running anymore. Why should it matter?"
"If you're leaving the country, the election doesn't matter, does it?"
"All right. I'm leaving in a week. I have to make sure my tracks are covered first."
entradas.menu: "All right. I'm leaving in a week. I have to make sure my tracks are covered first."

entradas.text: "All right. I'm leaving tomorrow."
entradas.menu: "All right. I'm leaving tomorrow."

entradas.text: "Dad, where are you going to go?"
I thought for a moment. Kyrute, the only truly neutral country I knew of, seemed like the obvious choice. A little house in the mountains wouldn't cost much.
"Kyrute. And you kids can visit whenever you want."
entradas.menu: "Kyrute. And you kids can visit whenever you want."

entradas.text: "I'd rather not tell you. For safety reasons."
entradas.menu: "I'd rather not tell you. For safety reasons."

entradas.text: "Then leave this house."
"It's the presidential complex. I'm the President, remember?"
entradas.menu: "It's the presidential complex. I'm the President, remember?"

entradas.text: "Fine. I will."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I will."

entradas.text: "Uh... All right."
"I guess good luck, then?"
Deana still looked slightly dazed.
"Yeah. Good luck, Papa."
Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
I drained my glass and left the table. I had packing to do.
Tears appeared in Monica's eyes.
"Please, Anton."
Franc and Deana watched silently as I got up from the table. Finally, Franc spoke up.
"Uh, I'll call you soon, Dad."
"Yeah. I will too!"
Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
I put that thought out of my mind as I left. I still had work to do.
"Anton, you can't do that. Not for my sake."
"It's not just for your sake. I'm sick and tired of this game. I want out."
entradas.menu: "It's not just for your sake. I'm sick and tired of this game. I want out."

entradas.text: "I can and I will."
entradas.menu: "I can and I will."

entradas.text: Monica sighed heavily.
"Franc, Deana -- your father and I are getting divorced."
"What a surprise."
"Kids, don't listen to her. Everything's going to work out."
entradas.menu: "Kids, don't listen to her. Everything's going to work out."

entradas.text: "I'm not surprised, Franc. He hasn't been living in the house for weeks."
"Monica, didn't you hear a word I said? I'm putting politics behind me so we can be a family again."
entradas.menu: "Monica, didn't you hear a word I said? I'm putting politics behind me so we can be a family again."

entradas.text: "Yeah, that was sarcasm."
"Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."
entradas.menu: "Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."

entradas.text: "That's not how this works. You don't get to choose."
"If you're retiring, why does it matter?"
"That was the plan before I learned the truth about what you'd done with your time in office. Along with the rest of Sordland."
"Mom, can't you give him a chance? Things were pretty good before, weren't they?"
"Oh, sweetheart. They were. But it's not that easy."
She turned to me, her eyes full of regret.
"I'm sorry, Anton. This dinner was a mistake. I think you should go."
"I will. And I'm dropping out of politics, no matter what."
entradas.menu: "I will. And I'm dropping out of politics, no matter what."

entradas.text: "Fine. But I'm not retiring. History will remember me as the best leader Sordland ever had."
entradas.menu: "Fine. But I'm not retiring. History will remember me as the best leader Sordland ever had."

entradas.text: "Uh, I guess... good luck, Dad."
"Yeah. Good luck!"
Franc and Deana were still sitting at the table, looking uncomfortable.
Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
I put that thought out of my mind as I made my way back to the guesthouse. I still had work to do.
Franc and Deana were still sitting at the table, looking uncomfortable.
"Uh, I guess... I'll call you soon, Dad."
"Yeah. I will too!"
I put that thought out of my mind as I made my way back to the guesthouse.
Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
Instead, I started thinking about how I would announce my decision to retire.
Monica sighed heavily.
"Franc, Deana -- your father and I are getting divorced."
"What a surprise."
"If you're retiring, why does it matter?"
"Uh, I guess... I'll call you soon, Dad."
"I'm not surprised, Franc. He hasn't been living in the house for weeks."
"Oh, sweetheart. They were. But it's not that easy."
"Yeah, that was sarcasm."
She turned to me, her eyes full of regret.
Franc and Deana were still sitting at the table, looking uncomfortable.
"Kids, don't listen to her. Everything's going to work out."
entradas.menu: "Kids, don't listen to her. Everything's going to work out."

"That was the plan before I learned the truth about what you'd done with your time in office. Along with the rest of Sordland."
"Mom, can't you give him a chance? Things were pretty good before, weren't they?"
"I'm sorry, Anton. This dinner was a mistake. I think you should go."
"I will. And I'm still dropping out of the election, no matter what."
entradas.menu: "I will. And I'm still dropping out of the election, no matter what."

entradas.text: "That's not how this works. You don't get to choose."
"This is the presidential complex. Last I checked, I was still President."
entradas.menu: "This is the presidential complex. Last I checked, I was still President."

Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
I put that thought out of my mind as I made my way back to the guesthouse.
Instead, I started thinking about where I wanted to go for my retirement.
Monica sighed heavily.
"Franc, Deana -- your father and I are getting divorced."
"What a surprise."
"I'm not surprised, Franc. He hasn't been living in the house for weeks."
"Don't worry, we won't make it public until then. I just wanted Franc and Deana to know."
"That was the plan before I learned the truth about what you'd done with your time in office. Along with the rest of Sordland."
"Yeah, that was sarcasm."
"Your mother is right, kids. We're getting divorced -- immediately after the election."
entradas.menu: "Your mother is right, kids. We're getting divorced -- immediately after the election."

entradas.text: "Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."
entradas.menu: "Monica, we were going to wait until after the election."

entradas.text: "Mom, can't you give him a chance? Maybe the next term really could be better."
"Oh, sweetheart. It's too late for that."
She turned to me, her eyes full of regret.
"I will. I'll see you later, kids."
entradas.menu: "I will. I'll see you later, kids."

entradas.text: "Uh, I guess... I'll call you soon, Dad."
Franc and Deana were still sitting at the table, looking uncomfortable.
"I'm sorry, Anton. This dinner was a mistake. I think you should go."
"This is the presidential complex. Last I checked, I was still President."

Monica refused to meet my gaze. I wondered if this was the last time I would see her -- or any of them.
I still had plenty of work to do.
"I swear to you all, I'll learn from my mistakes during the next administration."
entradas.menu: "I swear to you all, I'll learn from my mistakes during the next administration."

entradas.text: "I never thought I would be a pariah."
entradas.menu: "I never thought I would be a pariah."
